User story 2

Story 2 — Select a cruise destination

As a consumer, I want to select a cruise destination, so that I can search for cruises visiting a location that interests me.

Dependencies: US1 · shared controls and panel state

Scope: Home Page component; illustrative data and existing design-system assumptions.

Why it matters

Consumers can focus their search on places they want to visit.

Acceptance criteria

US2 · AC1#

AC1 — Display available destinations

Scenario: Open the Destination filter

Given the Find a Cruise component is displayed

When the consumer opens the Destination filter

Then the Destination panel expands below the filter row

And the selector displays the 16 supported destinations

And each displayed destination can be selected

US2 · AC2#

AC2 — Select a destination

Scenario: Select Alaska as the destination

Given the Destination filter is open

When the consumer selects "Alaska"

Then "Alaska" becomes the selected destination

And the filter displays "Alaska"

And "Any Destination" is no longer displayed

US2 · AC3#

AC3 — Change the destination

Scenario: Replace a selected destination

Given "Alaska" is the selected destination

When the consumer opens the Destination filter

And selects "Europe"

Then "Europe" replaces "Alaska"

And only "Europe" remains selected

US2 · AC4#

AC4 — Open only one filter panel at a time

Scenario: Open this filter while another filter is open

Given another filter panel is open

When the consumer opens this filter

Then the previously open panel closes

And any existing selection in that filter remains unchanged

And only this filter panel remains open

US2 · AC5#

AC5 — Reset to Any Destination

Proposed assumption — pending confirmation of individual filter reset; not an explicit requirement in the supplied brief.

Scenario: Remove this filter's current restriction

Given a destination is selected

When the consumer resets the Destination filter to its default value

Then the current destination selection is cleared

And the filter displays "Any Destination" and no longer restricts the search by this criterion

And the departure port and date selections remain unchanged

Decisions & open questions

Temporary assumptions are not confirmed answers. Blocking decisions must be resolved before production Engineering.

Blocking identifies a decision that must be resolved before the affected behavior is baselined or the story is accepted for production. It does not automatically block unrelated discovery or implementation work. Independent filter optionality and the minimum of one completed search criterion are separate assumptions.

Blocking questions and notes

Blocking

What is the authoritative source of the 16 destinations?

Decision owner / domain
Product Owner / Data Owner / Technical Lead
Temporary assumption
An existing API or managed configuration supplies the destination IDs and display names.
Source reasoning
Development requires authoritative values and identifiers.
Blocking

Is Destination single-select or multi-select?

Decision owner / domain
Product Owner
Temporary assumption
Only one destination may be selected.
Source reasoning
Cardinality affects the control, state model and search contract.
Blocking

Do the selected port or dates restrict the available destinations?

Decision owner / domain
Product Owner / Technical Lead
Temporary assumption
Destinations do not change dynamically. Compatibility is evaluated when searching.
Source reasoning
Cascading behavior would require additional data requests and invalidation rules.
Blocking

Should the consumer be able to reset Destination independently to "Any Destination"?

Decision owner / domain
Product Owner / UX Designer
Temporary assumption
Yes. Each filter is interpreted as individually optional, so its current selection can be removed independently and its unrestricted default restored without changing the other filters. This is an author assumption, not an explicit requirement in the supplied brief. US2 AC5 remains proposed until confirmed.
Source reasoning
If a filter is optional individually, selecting it should not make that restriction permanent. A consumer should be able to broaden the search again without reloading the page or losing other selections. Confirmation is blocking because it determines whether the reset transition and removal of this criterion from the search contract are required. Existing minimum-criteria validation remains unchanged.
Blocking scope
Blocks approval of the independent reset transition and its search-contract behavior, not unrelated filter work. The existing non-blocking question concerns the reset mechanism, conditional on reset being approved.

Non-blocking questions and notes

Non-blocking

How can the consumer return to Any Destination?

Decision owner / domain
Product Owner / UX Designer
Temporary assumption
The selector provides a clear action or unrestricted option.
Source reasoning
Consumers should be able to undo a selection without reloading the page.
Non-blocking

Can the panel be dismissed by clicking outside it or pressing Escape?

Decision owner / domain
UX Designer
Temporary assumption
Both actions close the panel without changing its current selection.
Source reasoning
These are conventional interaction behaviors.

If an answer changes, review the affected acceptance criteria, interaction states and tests before implementation.
